items.title: 67802_Charles Mingus oral history interview
items.q: And Art Tatum was a definite influence, because I had to work with him and study with him for a duet he always told me he wanted to get.

ctx.x: I think you may have said Jackie Brown, but say it again.

Whatever he did, I tried to learn. It was a different approach to the bass in jazz. Most guys go down one string, and slide into the next one, without using any of the positions across the instrument. To play the way he played, you had to do that way, to make speed, to get there in time. And Art Tatum was a definite influence, because I had to work with him and study with him for a duet he always told me he wanted to get. It was many years before I got to play with him in person, on a job which was in Miami,…

Having my ears come from Ellington, Charlie Parker. (Inaudible) I thought Charlie Parker's 2nd Bird was simpler, simpler to hear than Ellington, simpler than Art Tatum. I felt that guys who hadn't heard Duke Ellington, all the beboppers, for instance, or Art Tatum, would think that Charlie Parker was the most complicated, the most advanced lyrical lines going blowing in jazz. I never thought that.
